data_objects.name: hate_speech_annotations
data_objects.meaning: Tweets with annotator vote counts and a resolved hate/offensive/neither class.

data_objects.name: youtube_trending
data_objects.meaning: Daily trending-video observations with publication metadata, engagement counts, and moderation flags.

data_objects.name: airline_sentiment
data_objects.meaning: SQLite database with one Tweets table of US-airline tweets and sentiment annotations.

data_objects.name: bot_detection
data_objects.meaning: User/tweet records with account attributes and a binary bot label.

data_objects.name: gender_classifier
data_objects.meaning: Crowd-annotated Twitter profiles and tweets for profile-presence and gender classification.

data_objects.name: instagram_influencers
data_objects.meaning: Ranked Instagram influencer accounts with display-formatted reach, engagement, and like counts.

data_objects.name: synthetic_tweets
data_objects.meaning: Tweet-like records with account name, text, engagement counts, and timestamp.

data_objects.name: twitter_friend_graph
data_objects.meaning: Twitter user profiles with tags and adjacency lists of friend user IDs.
data_objects.notes: tags and friends are bracketed arrays embedded in CSV rows and require array-aware parsing.

variables.name: count
variables.meaning: Total annotator judgments represented by the vote columns.

variables.name: hate_speech
variables.meaning: Number of judgments assigning hate speech.

variables.name: offensive_language
variables.meaning: Number of judgments assigning offensive language.

variables.name: neither
variables.meaning: Number of judgments assigning neither hate nor offensive language.

variables.name: class
variables.meaning: Resolved numeric class label; source categories correspond to hate speech, offensive language, and neither.

variables.name: tweet
variables.meaning: Tweet text, including escaped entities and social-media syntax.

variables.name: video_id
variables.meaning: YouTube video identifier; a video can recur on multiple trending dates.

variables.name: trending_date
variables.meaning: Trending-list date stored in two-digit year.day.month form.

variables.name: publish_time
variables.meaning: Video publication timestamp in ISO-like UTC text.

variables.name: tags
variables.meaning: Video tags stored as pipe-delimited text; the source may use a placeholder for absent tags.

variables.name: views
variables.meaning: Cumulative views at the trending observation.

variables.name: likes
variables.meaning: Cumulative likes at the trending observation.

variables.name: dislikes
variables.meaning: Cumulative dislikes at the trending observation.

variables.name: comment_count
variables.meaning: Cumulative comments at the trending observation.

variables.name: video_error_or_removed
variables.meaning: Boolean flag indicating an unavailable or errored video.

variables.name: tweet_id
variables.meaning: Tweet identifier and SQLite primary key.

variables.name: airline_sentiment
variables.meaning: Resolved sentiment label such as positive, neutral, or negative.

variables.name: negativereason
variables.meaning: Categorized reason for negative sentiment; blank outside applicable rows.

variables.name: negativereason_confidence
variables.meaning: Confidence assigned to negativereason; may be blank.

variables.name: airline_sentiment_gold
variables.meaning: Gold sentiment annotation when supplied; otherwise blank.

variables.name: negativereason_gold
variables.meaning: Gold negative-reason annotation when supplied; otherwise blank.

variables.name: tweet_coord
variables.meaning: Coordinate text when supplied; often blank.

variables.name: tweet_created
variables.meaning: Tweet creation timestamp including timezone offset.

variables.name: Created At
variables.meaning: Account or record creation timestamp as stored.

variables.name: _golden
variables.meaning: Boolean indicator for a gold crowdsourcing unit.

variables.name: _last_judgment_at
variables.meaning: Timestamp of the last crowd judgment.

variables.name: gender:confidence
variables.meaning: Confidence for the resolved gender category.

variables.name: profile_yn
variables.meaning: Resolved yes/no indicator for whether the profile is classifiable/present.

variables.name: link_color
variables.meaning: Profile link color encoded as hexadecimal text.

variables.name: retweet_count
variables.meaning: Retweet count for the sampled tweet.

variables.name: sidebar_color
variables.meaning: Profile sidebar color encoded as hexadecimal text.

variables.name: tweet_id
variables.meaning: Tweet identifier; numeric parsing can lose integer precision.

variables.name: posts
variables.meaning: Post count stored with display suffixes such as k.

variables.name: followers
variables.meaning: Follower count stored with display suffixes such as m.

variables.name: avg_likes
variables.meaning: Average likes stored with display suffixes.

variables.name: 60_day_eng_rate
variables.meaning: 60-day engagement rate stored as percentage text.

variables.name: new_post_avg_like
variables.meaning: Average likes for new posts stored with display suffixes.

variables.name: total_likes
variables.meaning: Total likes stored with display suffixes such as b.

variables.name: Timestamp
variables.meaning: Record timestamp in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS form.

variables.name: tags
variables.meaning: Bracketed array of associated hashtag strings.

variables.name: lastSeen
variables.meaning: Last-seen time as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

variables.name: friends
variables.meaning: Bracketed adjacency list of friend user identifiers.

structure.description: youtube_trending is an event/snapshot table: video_id may repeat across trending_date as engagement counts evolve.
The airline sentiment SQLite file contains a single Tweets table keyed by tweet_id.
twitter_friend_graph represents a directed adjacency list from each row's id to the identifiers in friends; friendsCount is a separate declared count.
The eight objects are independent social-media collections with no declared cross-file identifier alignment.

uncertainties: Several files contain synthetic-looking text or display-formatted metrics, but source provenance is not declared in the files themselves.
Large social-media identifiers should be treated as strings to avoid floating-point precision loss.
twitter_friends.csv embeds comma-containing arrays in a layout that generic CSV parsers can misinterpret.
annotation_notes: All bounded source columns and the SQLite Tweets columns are annotated separately.
